prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element includes a shifting shaft, which can be rotated about an axis, an actuating body, which is connected to the shifting shaft for conjoint rotation and in an axially movable manner and which has at least two slotted guide sections designed as grooves on a peripheral surface, and a linear actuator, which is associated with the actuating body and has an actuatable actuator pin, which can engage in the slotted guide sections in order to axially move the actuating body. Each slotted guide section has an incoupling region for the actuator pin, an opposite outcoupling region for the actuator pin, and an adjusting region, which lies therebetween in the peripheral direction and is bent in a curved shape, for axially moving the actuating body. The incoupling region and the outcoupling region of the slotted guide sections that are adjacent in the peripheral direction are arranged at the same axial position.

outputs.L2: A device for adjusting a shifting element along its axis comprises a shifting shaft rotatable about an axis, and an actuating body coupled to the shifting shaft so that they rotate together while still allowing the actuating body to move axially. The actuating body has at least two slotted guide portions formed as grooves on its outer circumferential surface. A linear actuator is assigned to the actuating body and includes a controllable actuator pin that can enter the slotted guide portions to displace the actuating body in the axial direction. Each slotted guide portion includes an entry region for receiving the actuator pin, an opposing exit region for releasing the actuator pin, and an adjustment region located between them in the circumferential direction, the adjustment region being curved and serving to shift the actuating body axially. outputs.L3:
The apparatus is configured to axially adjust a shifting element by means of a rotatable shifting shaft. The shifting shaft serves as the primary rotary component and is operatively associated with the shifting element such that an axial displacement can be transmitted to the shifting element when required.

An actuating body is arranged on, or connected to, the shifting shaft. The actuating body is coupled to the shifting shaft for conjoint rotation, meaning that it rotates together with the shifting shaft without relative rotational movement between them. At the same time, the actuating body remains axially movable relative to the shifting shaft, so that it can be displaced along the longitudinal axis of the shifting shaft while still rotating with it.

On its peripheral surface, the actuating body is provided with at least two groove-like slotted guide sections. These slotted guide sections form guide tracks into which an actuator element can selectively engage. The guide sections are shaped so that, depending on the rotational position of the actuating body and the engagement of the actuator element, an axial movement of the actuating body can be generated.

A linear actuator is provided for producing this axial movement. The linear actuator includes an actuator pin that is movable toward and away from the actuating body. When the actuator pin is brought into engagement with one of the slotted guide sections, the rotation of the actuating body causes the actuator pin to follow the course of the respective guide section. As a result, the actuating body is displaced axially along the shifting shaft. This axial displacement is then used to adjust the shifting element.

Each of the slotted guide sections comprises several functional regions. These include an incoupling region, through which the actuator pin can enter the guide section, an outcoupling region, through which the actuator pin can leave the guide section, and a curved adjusting region arranged between them. The curved adjusting region is shaped so that, during relative movement between the actuator pin and the actuating body, an axial displacement of the actuating body is produced.

The incoupling and outcoupling regions of adjacent slotted guide sections are arranged at the same axial position. This configuration allows the actuator pin to transfer from one guide section to another in a controlled and reliable manner without requiring an additional axial offset during engagement or disengagement. As a result, the apparatus enables precise axial adjustment of the shifting element using a compact arrangement in which rotary motion of the shifting shaft is converted into axial displacement of the actuating body.
outputs.L4:
The apparatus is designed for the axial adjustment of a shifting element, in particular within a transmission or comparable mechanical assembly. It comprises a shifting shaft that is mounted so as to be rotatable about its longitudinal axis, and an actuating body that is arranged on or coupled to the shifting shaft in such a way that it can be displaced in the axial direction. The actuating body acts on the shifting element, so that an axial movement of the actuating body produces a corresponding adjustment or shifting movement of the shifting element.

To generate the axial movement, the actuating body is provided with a plurality of slotted guide sections. These slotted guide sections are formed as grooves, tracks, or guide paths extending over the circumference of the actuating body. A linear actuator is assigned to the actuating body and has an actuator pin that can be moved in a substantially linear direction. The actuator pin is configured to engage selectively in the grooves of the slotted guide sections. When the shifting shaft and the actuating body rotate relative to the actuator pin, the engagement of the actuator pin in a slotted guide section converts the rotational movement into an axial displacement of the actuating body. In this manner, the actuator pin and the grooved guide sections cooperate to move the shifting element into different axial positions.

Each slotted guide section may include an incoupling region, in which the actuator pin enters or is guided into the respective groove, and an outcoupling region, in which the actuator pin leaves or is guided out of the groove. Between these regions, the guide contour of the groove determines the axial travel of the actuating body. Depending on the inclination, curvature, or axial offset of the groove, the actuating body may be shifted in one axial direction, held in a defined axial position, or shifted back in the opposite axial direction.

A significant feature of the apparatus is the arrangement of adjacent slotted guide sections. In particular, the outcoupling region of one slotted guide section and the incoupling region of an adjacent slotted guide section are positioned at the same axial level or axial position. As a result, the actuator pin can transition from one guide section to the next without requiring an additional axial compensation movement or abrupt displacement of the actuating body. This coordinated arrangement allows the actuator pin to disengage from one groove and engage the neighboring groove in a controlled manner while the actuating body remains axially aligned.

By placing the incoupling and outcoupling regions of adjacent slotted guide sections at the same axial position, the apparatus achieves a smoother and more reliable shifting operation. The actuator pin can be coupled into and out of the guide sections with reduced mechanical stress, lower risk of jamming, and improved synchronization between the rotational position of the shifting shaft and the axial position of the actuating body. This can reduce wear on the grooves and on the actuator pin, improve shifting precision, and allow compact construction of the shifting mechanism.

The apparatus therefore provides a simple and effective way to transform rotational motion of a shifting shaft into controlled axial motion of a shifting element. The combination of the rotatable shifting shaft, the axially movable actuating body, the grooved slotted guide sections, and the linearly movable actuator pin enables precise positioning of the shifting element. At the same time, the special arrangement of the incoupling and outcoupling regions of neighboring guide sections ensures coordinated engagement of the actuator pin and contributes to smooth, dependable axial adjustment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an apparatus that axially adjusts a shifting element using a rotating shifting shaft, an axially movable actuating body with grooved slotted guide sections, and a linear actuator pin engaging the grooves.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element includes a shifting shaft mounted for rotation about a shaft axis and operatively coupled to the shifting element, an actuating body arranged coaxially with or adjacent to the shifting shaft and movable in an axial direction, and at least one slotted guide section formed in the actuating body. The slotted guide section includes a groove having a predetermined guide profile extending at least partially obliquely relative to the axial direction. A linear actuator includes an actuator pin configured to engage the groove and to move along a substantially linear actuating path. Linear movement of the actuator pin within the groove displaces the actuating body axially, thereby rotating the shifting shaft or controlling its axial shifting position to adjust the shifting element between selected operating positions. The groove profile may define a plurality of guide regions corresponding to discrete shift positions and may provide mechanical guidance, locking, or detent functionality during adjustment of the shifting element.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.output: A gearbox shifting mechanism includes a rotatable shift shaft carrying an actuating body having a plurality of peripheral groove guide sections. A linear actuator includes an actuator pin movable toward and away from the actuating body to selectively couple with one of the peripheral groove guide sections. Axial displacement of the actuator pin while coupled to a selected groove guide section causes rotation of the actuating body and the shift shaft to execute a corresponding gear shift operation. Adjacent peripheral groove guide sections include respective coupling regions positioned at a common axial location on the actuating body, such that the actuator pin can be selectively introduced into either of the adjacent groove guide sections from the same axial actuator position.
